questions.stem: What is the focus of Business Modelling?
options: The business itself: how value is created, how work flows, who is involved and how decisions are made
The design of databases and tables
questions.explanation: Business Modelling focuses not on data, databases or systems but on the business itself and how it achieves its objectives.

questions.stem: What is the main goal of Business Modelling?
options: To define primary and foreign keys
To provide a complete and holistic view of the business
questions.explanation: The main goal is a complete and holistic view of the business, which makes it easier to align operations, decisions and systems with strategic goals.

questions.stem: Which two questions does Business Modelling concentrate on?
options: The what and the how of the business
questions.explanation: Business Modelling concentrates on the what and the how of the business, looking at processes, roles, responsibilities, rules and policies.

questions.stem: Where does Business Modelling usually sit in the sequence of modelling activities?
options: Only after systems have gone live
Between logical and physical data modelling
As the first step before information modelling and data modelling
It is done last, as documentation
questions.explanation: Business Modelling is usually the first step before moving into information modelling and data modelling.

questions.stem: In the school example of Business Modelling, what does the description deliberately NOT include?
options: The teacher checking the answer sheet
The principal looking at overall performance
Marks tables, student databases or report formats
questions.explanation: The school example describes the process, people and decisions but not marks tables, student databases or report formats.

questions.stem: In the loan approval example, who decides whether to approve or reject the loan?
questions.explanation: In the operational view, a risk manager decides whether to approve or reject the loan after the credit department checks credit history.

questions.stem: In the loan approval example, which team monitors repayments after funds are released?
questions.explanation: The finance team releases the funds and the collections team later monitors repayments.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the analytical side that Business Modelling connects to daily operations?
options: Managers analysing approval and rejection rates, average loan amounts or repayment behaviour
questions.explanation: Business Modelling links operational activities with analytical outcomes such as approval rates, loan amounts and repayment trends.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the nature of Business Modelling?
options: It is detailed, technical and tool-specific
It is high-level, strategic and independent of technology and tools
It is concerned mainly with database performance
It is a low-level description of individual tasks
It is only used by IT departments
questions.explanation: Business Modelling is high-level and strategic in nature, independent of technology and tools, and avoids technical details.

questions.stem: Why does Business Modelling act as the baseline for all other modelling techniques?
options: Because it defines the physical schema first
Because it tells the story of the business so information and data models are grounded in real needs rather than assumptions
Because it selects the database vendor
Because it produces the final reports
Because it replaces the need for data modelling
questions.explanation: Once the story of the business is understood, information models and data models can be designed with confidence, grounded in real business needs.
